164	  the change history against it must reproduce `grid`.
165	- `tick` — number of ticks already executed.
166	- `robots` — list of `{"robot_id", "position", "route", "task_id",
167	  "distance_travelled"}`; `position` is `[x, y]` and `route` is the remaining
168	  waypoints after the current position (empty for a paused robot).
169	- `tasks` — list of `{"task_id", "pickup", "dropoff", "assigned_robot",
170	  "picked_up", "completed"}`. Completed tasks keep their historical
171	  `assigned_robot`; unassigned tasks use `null`.
172	- `paused_tasks` — ids of tasks whose assigned robot currently cannot reach a
173	  required point on the saved map.
174	- `traffic_waits` — optional list of `{"robot_id", "blocked_by", "ticks"}`
175	  entries: robots currently held up by other robots, who blocks them, and for
176	  how many consecutive ticks. Older files without this field load with every
177	  counter at zero.
178	- `map_changes` — every actual edit in order, each
179	  `{"tick", "sequence", "added", "removed"}`; `sequence` runs from 1 and
180	  consecutive edits at the same `tick` preserve their order.
181	- `replay` — ordered events. Tick frames are `{"type": "tick", "tick", "moved",
182	  "robots", "completed"}`, numbered consecutively from `1` through `tick`.
183	  Map-change frames are interspersed at their effective tick and have the shape
184	  `{"type": "map_change", "tick", "sequence", "added", "removed"}`. In any
185	  non-zero-tick file the last tick frame's robot positions must equal the
186	  current robot positions; historical frames are never overwritten by later
187	  maps.
188	
189	Loading validates the entire document: corrupted JSON, missing or wrongly
190	typed fields, unsupported versions, duplicate robot or task ids, overlapping
191	or out-of-bounds/blocked robot positions, routes that leave the map, cross
192	obstacles, or make non-adjacent moves, task/robot ownership mismatches, a
193	broken replay history, out-of-bounds or add/remove-conflicting change records,
194	a change history that does not reproduce the saved grid, and an inconsistent
195	paused-task state are all rejected. So is a replay whose *history* could never
196	have happened, even when its final frame matches the saved robots: a robot out
197	of bounds or on an obstacle that existed at that tick, two robots sharing a
198	cell at a tick boundary, a jump of more than one orthogonal cell or a two-robot
199	cell swap between neighboring tick frames, and a `moved` list that names an
200	unknown/duplicated robot or does not exactly match the robots that changed
201	position (following another robot into the cell it just vacated is legal, and
202	the list need not be sorted). Map edits are judged against contemporary
203	positions: a cell a robot once passed through may be closed later without
204	invalidating the replay, a robot may not appear in a cell before it opens, and
205	an edit may not add an obstacle onto a cell occupied when that tick ended —
206	not even if another edit of the same tick removes it again. The first tick

209	empty fleets and all-waiting frames remain valid. Version 1 documents contain
210	tick frames without a `type` field and none of the edit-related keys; they

# Warehouse Robot Fleet Simulator

A small, deterministic Python simulator for experimenting with warehouse maps,

efficiency metrics. It runs locally and has no runtime dependencies outside the

## Quick start

```bash
python3 -m warehouse_fleet demo --steps 12
```

The command builds a sample grid, assigns pickup-and-delivery tasks to available
robots, advances the fleet one tick at a time, and prints a JSON replay summary.

Run the tests with:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The public Python API exposes `GridMap`, `Robot`, `Task`, `FleetSimulator`, and
`shortest_path` for programmatic scenarios.

## Closing and reopening cells at runtime

Between ticks you may change the map with one batch call. The edit takes effect
immediately but neither advances the clock, moves a robot, nor adds mileage:

```python
simulator.modify_obstacles(added=[(3, 2), (3, 3)], removed=[(5, 4)])
```

Coordinates must be plain two-integer pairs (booleans are not integers). The
whole request is validated up front and rejected with `ValueError` if a
coordinate is out of bounds or malformed, a cell is both added and removed, or
a newly added obstacle covers a robot's current cell; on rejection the map,
routes, tasks, statistics and history are all left untouched. Duplicate
coordinates inside one batch are processed once; adding an already blocked
cell or removing a traversable cell is a no-op, and a batch with no actual
effect produces no change record.

After an accepted edit every assigned, unfinished task keeps its robot. A robot
that has not picked up replans a shortest feasible route from its current cell
through the pickup point to the dropoff (a robot already at the pickup point
collects first at the next step); a robot carrying goods routes straight to the
dropoff and never returns to a subsequently closed pickup cell. If any required
cell is unreachable, the robot's remaining route is cleared and the task is
*paused* — it is neither driven along a stale route, released, nor completed.
Unassigned tasks whose points are unreachable simply keep waiting and never
block other tasks. The next `step()` after cells reopen automatically resumes
paused driving and assigns waiting tasks; collision avoidance still applies and
robots never enter a new obstacle.

Queries and history:

```python
simulator.status()              # current obstacles + paused task ids + traffic waits
simulator.map_change_history()  # effective tick, adds/removes, order
```

`status()` reports tasks paused because the map made their route infeasible,
which is distinct from a robot briefly waiting for another robot to clear the
way. Every *actual* change is stored both in the dedicated history and in the
replay as a `map_change` event carrying the tick it took effect at, its global
sequence number (consecutive edits at the same tick keep their order), and the
added/removed cells; ordinary tick frames keep their original positions and
completion data and are never rewritten by later maps. Identical initial state
with an identical sequence of steps and edits always produces identical
routes, replay and statistics.

## Automatic yielding in traffic

When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, `step()` no longer
just waits: an idle blocker is asked to step onto a free neighbouring cell
that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy robot whose blocker cannot
drive on may sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself and replan its
(still shortest) route from there. Every robot still moves at most one
orthogonal cell per tick (or waits), robots never share a cell at the end of
a tick, never swap places within one tick, and never enter an obstacle.

A sidestep that cannot make progress is not taken. If the replanned route
steps straight back through the cell the robot is vacating, still runs past
the same blocker's cell, and the blocker cannot use the opening to get out of
the way (for example an idle robot parked at the end of a one-wide corridor
with no neighbouring cell to yield onto), the robot waits instead of
retreating and shuttling back to the identical blockage on the next tick.
More empty cells behind the waiting robot do not change this. A sidestep that
genuinely routes around the blocker, or a retreat the blocker immediately
drives into to clear the way, is still driven.

Yielding moves count as mileage; waiting does not. The task keeps its
original robot and the pickup rules are unchanged — goods are collected
before delivery, a loaded robot never returns to the pickup cell, and nothing
completes early because of a detour. Robots paused by map unreachability stay
put and never take part in yielding. An idle robot that yields is not hired
by doing so: it stays on its side cell once the way is clear and can still
pick up tasks later. If no safe side cell exists, both robots simply wait —
time advances, cargo and tasks are kept, and nothing collides or completes.

Traffic waits are reported separately from map pauses:

```python
simulator.status()["traffic_waits"]
# [{"robot_id": "R-01", "blocked_by": ["R-02"], "ticks": 3}, ...]
```

A robot's counter only grows while it stops for traffic and another robot
still blocks its next waypoint once the tick's moves have settled; any move or
the blockage clearing resets it to zero. A blocker that advances later in the
same tick is not a blockage at tick end, so that tick adds nothing. If the
wait never breaks but the robot holding the next cell merely changes, the
count continues with the new blocker; once the wait was actually interrupted,
a later blockage starts again at one. The
same report appears in `metrics()` (and therefore in the command-line
output), and it is saved into and restored from checkpoints — older
checkpoint files without it load with every counter at zero.


## Saving and resuming progress

State can be saved after any tick and resumed later in a new process. From
Python, `FleetSimulator.save_checkpoint(path)` writes the state without
advancing the tick or mutating the simulator, and the class method
`FleetSimulator.load_checkpoint(path)` returns an independent simulator:

interfere with each other.

```python
simulator.save_checkpoint("fleet.json")

```

complete old contents or the complete new contents, and a failed save to a new


updated state; without it the source file is left untouched, and naming the

- `tasks` — list of `{"task_id", "pickup", "dropoff", "assigned_robot",

- `paused_tasks` — ids of tasks whose assigned robot currently cannot reach a
  required point on the saved map.
- `traffic_waits` — optional list of `{"robot_id", "blocked_by", "ticks"}`
  entries: robots currently held up by other robots, who blocks them, and for
  how many consecutive ticks. Older files without this field load with every

  non-zero-tick file the last tick frame's robot positions must equal the
  current robot positions; historical frames are never overwritten by later

Loading validates the entire document: corrupted JSON, missing or wrongly
typed fields, unsupported versions, duplicate robot or task ids, overlapping

obstacles, or make non-adjacent moves, task/robot ownership mismatches, a
broken replay history, out-of-bounds or add/remove-conflicting change records,
a change history that does not reproduce the saved grid, and an inconsistent

have happened, even when its final frame matches the saved robots: a robot out
of bounds or on an obstacle that existed at that tick, two robots sharing a
cell at a tick boundary, a jump of more than one orthogonal cell or a two-robot
cell swap between neighboring tick frames, and a `moved` list that names an
unknown/duplicated robot or does not exactly match the robots that changed
position (following another robot into the cell it just vacated is legal, and
the list need not be sorted). Map edits are judged against contemporary
positions: a cell a robot once passed through may be closed later without
invalidating the replay, a robot may not appear in a cell before it opens, and
an edit may not add an obstacle onto a cell occupied when that tick ended —
not even if another edit of the same tick removes it again. The first tick

1	"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.
2	
3	Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
4	:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
5	deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
6	event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
7	never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
8	information recorded at the time.
9	
10	Automatic yielding
11	------------------
12	When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
13	keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: an idle blocker is asked to
14	move onto a free side cell that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy
15	robot facing a blocker that cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free
16	adjacent cell and replan its (still shortest) route from there. A retreat that
17	only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
18	replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
19	blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
20	corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
21	empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Yield moves count as
22	mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
23	completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
24	takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
25	time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
26	purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
27	blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
28	:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
29	map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
30	end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
31	asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
32	made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
33	and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
34	tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
35	blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
36	identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
37	interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
38	reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
39	longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
40	entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
41	or increments one.
42	
43	Checkpoint file format
44	----------------------
45	``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
46	version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.
47	
48	``version``
49	    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
50	``grid``
51	    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
52	    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
53	``tick``
54	    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
55	    loading never advance this value.
56	``robots``
57	    List of robot states, each
58	    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
59	    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
60	    remaining waypoints after ``position``.
61	``tasks``
62	    List of task states, each
63	    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
64	    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
65	    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``.
66	``replay``
67	    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
68	    through ``tick`` and have the shape
69	    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
70	    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
71	    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
72	    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
73	    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
74	    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
75	    robot positions.
76	``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
77	    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
78	    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
79	``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
80	    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
81	    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
82	    ``grid``.
83	``traffic_waits`` (optional)
84	    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
85	    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
86	    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
87	    wait counter at zero.
88	
89	Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
90	``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
91	baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.
92	
93	Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
94	fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
95	bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
96	mismatches, broken replay or map-change history, and a history that does not
97	reproduce the saved grid all raise :class:`ValueError`.
98	
99	The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
100	for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
101	cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
102	robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
103	may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
104	cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
105	fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
106	duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
107	robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
108	applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
109	robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
110	cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
111	frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
112	it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
113	"""
114

132	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
133	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
134	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

137	def _as_cell(value: object, description: str) -> Position:
138	    """Validate a user supplied coordinate as a two-integer pair."""
139	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
140	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
141	    if len(value) != 2:
142	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
143	    if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
144	        raise ValueError(f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types")
145	    return value[0], value[1]
146	
147	
148	def _as_pair(value: object, description: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
149	    if (
150	        not isinstance(value, list)
151	        or len(value) != 2
152	        or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
153	    ):
154	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
155	    return value[0], value[1]

158	class FleetSimulator:
159	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
160	        self.grid = grid
161	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
162	        # replayed against this baseline.
163	        self.base_grid = grid
164	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
165	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
166	        self.tick = 0
167	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
168	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
169	        self._map_sequence = 0
170	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
171	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
172	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
173	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
174	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
175	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
176	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
177	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
178	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
179	
180	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
181	    # Dynamic map edits
182	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
183	
184	    def modify_obstacles(
185	        self,
186	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
187	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
188	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
189	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
190	
191	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
192	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
193	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
194	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
195	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
196	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
197	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
198	
199	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
200	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
201	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
202	        distance is accumulated.
203	        """
204	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
205	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
206	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
207	        if conflict:
208	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
209	            raise ValueError(
210	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
211	            )
212	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
213	        for cell in add_cells:
214	            if cell in occupied:
215	                raise ValueError(
216	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
217	                )
218	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
219	
220	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
221	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
222	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
223	        seen: set[Position] = set()
224	        ordered: list[Position] = []
225	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
226	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
227	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
228	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
229	            if position in seen:
230	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
231	                continue
232	            seen.add(position)
233	            ordered.append(position)
234	        return ordered
235	
236	    def _apply_map_change(
237	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
238	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
239	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
240	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
241	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
242	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
243	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
244	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
245	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
246	
247	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
248	        # known to change the map.
249	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
250	        self._map_sequence += 1
251	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
252	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
253	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
254	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
255	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
256	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
257	
258	    def _map_change_record(
259	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
260	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
261	        return {
262	            "type": "map_change",
263	            "tick": self.tick,
264	            "sequence": sequence,
265	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
266	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
267	        }
268	
269	    def _plan_route(
270	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
271	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
272	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
273	
274	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
275	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first.
276	        """
277	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
278	        try:
279	            if not task.picked_up:
280	                if origin == task.pickup:
281	                    to_pickup: list[Position] = []
282	                else:
283	                    to_pickup = shortest_path(self.grid, origin, task.pickup)
284	                to_dropoff = shortest_path(self.grid, task.pickup, task.dropoff)
285	            else:
286	                # Goods are already on board: a reclosed pickup cell must not
287	                # pull the robot back.
288	                to_pickup = []
289	                to_dropoff = shortest_path(self.grid, origin, task.dropoff)
290	        except ValueError:
291	            return None
292	        return to_pickup + to_dropoff
293	
294	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
295	        for task in self.tasks.values():
296	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
297	                continue
298	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
299	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
300	                continue
301	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
302	            if route is None:
303	                robot.route = []
304	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
305	            else:
306	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
307	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
308	                robot.route = route
309	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
310	
311	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
312	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
313	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
314	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
315	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
316	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
317	                continue
318	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
319	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
320	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
321	                continue
322	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
323	            if route is None:
324	                robot.route = []
325	                continue
326	            robot.route = route
327	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
328	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
329	
330	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
331	    # Traffic conflicts and yielding
332	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
333	
334	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
335	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
336	        cells: set[Position] = set()
337	        for robot in self.robots.values():
338	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
339	                cells.update(robot.route)
340	        return cells
341	
342	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
343	        self,
344	        blocker: Robot,
345	        requester: Robot,
346	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
347	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
348	    ) -> Position | None:
349	        """Free side-cell an idle blocker can yield to, or None.
350	
351	        The target may not be the requester's own cell (that would swap the
352	        two robots within one tick) nor any cell another robot still plans to
353	        drive through, so the blocker never trades one blockage for another.
354	        """
355	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
356	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
357	            if cell == requester.position:
358	                continue
359	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
360	                continue
361	            if cell in on_routes:
362	                continue
363	            return cell
364	        return None
365	
366	    def _self_sidestep(
367	        self,
368	        robot: Robot,
369	        task: Task | None,
370	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
371	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
372	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
373	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
374	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
375	
376	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
377	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
378	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
379	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
380	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
381	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
382	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
383	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
384	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
385	        """
386	        if task is None or task.completed:
387	            return None
388	        destination = robot.route[0]
389	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
390	        if blocker_id is None:
391	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
392	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id)
393	        best: tuple[int, int, Position, list[Position]] | None = None
394	        for index, cell in enumerate(self.grid.neighbors(robot.position)):
395	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved or cell in on_routes:
396	                continue
397	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
398	            if route is None:
399	                continue
400	            if (
401	                blocker_id is not None
402	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
403	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
404	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
405	                )
406	            ):
407	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
408	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
409	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
410	                continue
411	            if best is None or (len(route), index) < (best[0], best[1]):
412	                best = (len(route), index, cell, route)
413	        if best is None:
414	            return None
415	        return best[2], best[3]
416	
417	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
418	        self,
419	        robot: Robot,
420	        side: Position,
421	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
422	        blocker_id: str,
423	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
424	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
425	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
426	    ) -> bool:
427	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
428	
429	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
430	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
431	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
432	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
433	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
434	        never rejected here.
435	        """
436	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
437	            return False
438	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
439	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
440	            return False
441	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
442	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
443	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
444	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
445	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
446	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
447	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
448	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
449	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
450	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
451	        return not self._can_vacate(
452	            blocker,
453	            robot,
454	            hyp_occupied,
455	            reserved,
456	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
457	            blocked_path,
458	        )
459	
460	    def _can_vacate(
461	        self,
462	        blocker: Robot,
463	        requester: Robot,
464	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
465	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
466	        checking: frozenset[str],
467	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
468	    ) -> bool:
469	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
470	
471	        An idle blocker leaves only by yielding onto a safe side cell for the
472	        requesting robot; a busy blocker leaves by driving onto its next
473	        waypoint (possibly following a chain of robots that all move this tick)
474	        or by sidestepping onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by
475	        map unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave
476	        check is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
477	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
478	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive back
479	        through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so such
480	        sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on the
481	        blocker's own route does).
482	        """
483	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
484	            return False
485	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
486	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
487	            return False
488	        if task is not None and not blocker.route:
489	            # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this tick;
490	            # it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
491	            return False
492	        if task is None:
493	            # Idle robots only ever move by yielding for a requester.
494	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
495	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
496	        if blocker.route:
497	            ahead = blocker.route[0]
498	            if (
499	                self.grid.traversable(ahead)
500	                and ahead not in occupied
501	                and ahead not in reserved
502	            ):
503	                return True
504	            occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
505	            if (
506	                occupant_id is not None
507	                and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
508	                and occupant_id not in checking
509	            ):
510	                # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
511	                # vacates its cell this same tick.
512	                if self._can_vacate(
513	                    self.robots[occupant_id],
514	                    requester,
515	                    occupied,
516	                    reserved,
517	                    checking | {blocker.robot_id},
518	                    blocked_path,
519	                ):
520	                    return True
521	        # Otherwise the blocker might sidestep onto a free side cell itself,
522	        # but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has to use.
523	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
524	        for side_cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
525	            if (
526	                side_cell in occupied
527	                or side_cell in reserved
528	                or side_cell in on_routes
529	                or side_cell in blocked_path
530	            ):
531	                continue
532	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
533	                return True
534	        return False
535	
536	    def _update_traffic_waits(
537	        self,
538	        waited: dict[str, str],
539	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
540	    ) -> None:
541	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
542	
543	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
544	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
545	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
546	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
547	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
548	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
549	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
550	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
551	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
552	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
553	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
554	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
555	        """
556	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
557	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
558	        for robot_id in waited:
559	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
560	                continue
561	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
562	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
563	                continue
564	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
565	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
566	                continue
567	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
568	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
569	                continue
570	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
571	            if entry is None:
572	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
573	            else:
574	                surviving[robot_id] = {
575	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
576	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
577	                }
578	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
579	
580	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
581	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
582	
583	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
584	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
585	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
586	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
587	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
588	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
589	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
590	        """
591	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
592	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
593	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
594	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
595	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
596	                continue
597	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
598	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
599	
600	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
601	        return [
602	            {
603	                "robot_id": robot_id,
604	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
605	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
606	            }
607	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
608	        ]

614	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
615	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
616	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
617	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
618	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
619	            for robot in self.robots.values():
620	                if not robot.idle:
621	                    continue
622	                try:
623	                    route = shortest_path(self.grid, robot.position, task.pickup)
624	                    route += shortest_path(self.grid, task.pickup, task.dropoff)
625	                except ValueError:
626	                    continue
627	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
628	            if not choices:
629	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
630	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
631	                continue
632	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
633	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
634	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
635	            robot.route = route
636	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
637	
638	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
639	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
640	        for robot in self.robots.values():
641	            if robot.task_id is None:
642	                continue
643	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
644	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
645	                task.picked_up = True
646	
647	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
648	        self._confirm_pickups()
649	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
650	        self.assign_tasks()
651	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
652	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
653	        self._confirm_pickups()
654	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
655	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
656	        moved: list[str] = []
657	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
658	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
659	
660	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
661	            del occupied[robot.position]
662	            robot.position = destination
663	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
664	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
665	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
666	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
667	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
668	
669	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
670	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
671	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
672	                continue
673	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
674	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
675	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
676	                continue
677	            if not robot.route:
678	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
679	                continue
680	            destination = robot.route[0]
681	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
682	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
683	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
684	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
685	                    if route is None:
686	                        robot.route = []
687	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
688	                    else:
689	                        robot.route = route
690	                continue
691	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
692	            if blocker_id is None:
693	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
694	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
695	                relocate(robot, destination)
696	                robot.route.pop(0)
697	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
698	                continue
699	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
700	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
701	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
702	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
703	                if blocker.task_id is None:
704	                    # Idle blocker: ask it to yield onto a free side cell,
705	                    # then take over the cell it vacated.
706	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
707	                    if side is not None:
708	                        relocate(blocker, side)
709	                        relocate(robot, destination)
710	                        robot.route.pop(0)
711	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
712	                        continue
713	                elif blocker.route:
714	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
715	                    if (
716	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
717	                        and ahead not in occupied
718	                        and ahead not in reserved
719	                    ):
720	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
721	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
722	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
723	                        continue
724	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
725	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
726	            side = self._self_sidestep(
727	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
728	            )
729	            if side is not None:
730	                cell, route = side
731	                relocate(robot, cell)
732	                robot.route = route
733	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
734	                continue
735	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
736	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
737	        self.tick += 1
738	        event: dict[str, object] = {
739	            "type": "tick",
740	            "tick": self.tick,
741	            "moved": moved,
742	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
743	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
744	        }
745	        self.replay.append(event)
746	        return event
747	
748	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
749	        if robot.task_id is None:
750	            return
751	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
752	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
753	            return
754	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
755	            task.picked_up = True
756	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
757	            task.completed = True
758	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
759	            robot.task_id = None

762	        completed = sum(task.completed for task in self.tasks.values())
763	        return {
764	            "ticks": self.tick,
765	            "tasks_total": len(self.tasks),
766	            "tasks_completed": completed,
767	            "tasks_paused": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
768	            "completion_ratio": completed / len(self.tasks) if self.tasks else 1.0,
769	            "distance_total": sum(robot.distance_travelled for robot in self.robots.values()),
770	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
771	        }

801	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
802	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
803	
804	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
805	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
806	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
807	        raise :class:`OSError`.
808	        """
809	        document = {
810	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
811	            "grid": {
812	                "width": self.grid.width,
813	                "height": self.grid.height,
814	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
815	            },
816	            "base_grid": {
817	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
818	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
819	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
820	            },
821	            "tick": self.tick,
822	            "robots": [
823	                {
824	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
825	                    "position": list(robot.position),
826	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
827	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
828	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
829	                }
830	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
831	            ],
832	            "tasks": [
833	                {
834	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
835	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
836	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
837	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
838	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
839	                    "completed": task.completed,
840	                }
841	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
842	            ],
843	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
844	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
845	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
846	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
847	        }
848	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
849	
850	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
851	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
852	        try:
853	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
854	            try:
855	                handle.write(payload)
856	                handle.flush()
857	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
858	            finally:
859	                handle.close()
860	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
861	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
862	        except BaseException:
863	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
864	            try:
865	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
866	            except OSError:
867	                pass
868	            raise
869	
870	    @staticmethod
871	    def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
872	        try:
873	            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
874	        except OSError:
875	            return
876	        try:
877	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
878	        except OSError:
879	            pass
880	        finally:
881	            os.close(dir_fd)

883	    @classmethod
884	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
885	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
886	
887	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
888	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
889	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
890	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
891	        """
892	        try:
893	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
894	                text = handle.read()
895	        except OSError:
896	            raise
897	        try:
898	            data = json.loads(text)
899	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
900	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc
901	        return cls._from_checkpoint(data)

903	    @classmethod
904	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
905	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
906	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
907	
908	        version = data.get("version")
909	        if not _is_int(version):
910	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
911	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
912	            raise ValueError(
913	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
914	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
915	            )
916	
917	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
918	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
919	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
920	
921	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
922	        paused: set[str] = set()
923	        if version == 1:
924	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
925	            base_grid = grid
926	        else:
927	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
928	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
929	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
930	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
931	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
932	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
933	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
934	
935	        robots: list[Robot] = []
936	        for record in robot_records:
937	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
938	            if not grid.traversable(position):
939	                raise ValueError(
940	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
941	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
942	                )
943	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
944	            previous = position
945	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
946	                waypoint = _as_pair(
947	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
948	                )
949	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
950	                    raise ValueError(
951	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
952	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
953	                    )
954	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
955	                    raise ValueError(
956	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
957	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
958	                    )
959	                route.append(waypoint)
960	                previous = waypoint
961	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
962	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
963	                raise ValueError(
964	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
965	                    "non-negative integer"
966	                )
967	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
968	
969	        tasks: list[Task] = []
970	        for record in task_records:
971	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
972	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
973	            tasks.append(
974	                Task(
975	                    record["task_id"],
976	                    pickup,
977	                    dropoff,
978	                    record["assigned_robot"],
979	                    record["picked_up"],
980	                    record["completed"],
981	                )
982	            )
983	
984	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
985	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
986	
987	        for robot in robots:
988	            if robot.task_id is not None:
989	                task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
990	                if task is None:
991	                    raise ValueError(
992	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task {robot.task_id!r}"
993	                    )
994	                if task.completed:
995	                    raise ValueError(
996	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} that is "
997	                        "already completed"
998	                    )
999	                if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
1000	                    raise ValueError(
1001	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} but the "
1002	                        f"task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
1003	                    )
1004	        for task in tasks:
1005	            if task.completed and not task.picked_up:
1006	                raise ValueError(f"task {task.task_id!r} is completed but never picked up")
1007	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
1008	                raise ValueError(
1009	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
1010	                )
1011	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are free
1012	            # to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a task is
1013	            # still in progress.
1014	            if not task.completed and task.assigned_robot is not None:
1015	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
1016	                if owner is None:
1017	                    raise ValueError(
1018	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
1019	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
1020	                    )
1021	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
1022	                    raise ValueError(
1023	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} but the "
1024	                        f"robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
1025	                    )
1026	
1027	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1028	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1029	
1030	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1031	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
1032	            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")
1033	
1034	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1035	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1036	        simulator.tick = tick
1037	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1038	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1039	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1040	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1041	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits
1042	        # Version 1 has no edit history: its saved grid is the baseline and
1043	        # applies to every tick frame. Version 2 replays the recorded changes
1044	        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
1045	        # map.
1046	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
1047	        return simulator

1049	    @staticmethod
1050	    def _require_field(data: Mapping[str, object], field_name: str) -> object:
1051	        if field_name not in data:
1052	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is missing required field {field_name!r}")
1053	        return data[field_name]

1055	    @classmethod
1056	    def _load_grid(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> GridMap:
1057	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "grid")
1058	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
1059	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'grid' must be an object")
1060	        width = raw.get("width")
1061	        height = raw.get("height")
1062	        if not _is_int(width) or width <= 0:
1063	            raise ValueError("checkpoint grid width must be a positive integer")
1064	        if not _is_int(height) or height <= 0:
1065	            raise ValueError("checkpoint grid height must be a positive integer")
1066	        raw_obstacles = raw.get("obstacles")
1067	        if not isinstance(raw_obstacles, list):
1068	            raise ValueError("checkpoint grid 'obstacles' must be a list")
1069	        obstacles: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
1070	        for index, cell in enumerate(raw_obstacles):

1195	    @classmethod
1196	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1197	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
1198	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1199	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
1200	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1201	        last_tick = -1
1202	        last_sequence = 0
1203	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
1204	            context = f"map change {index}"
1205	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
1206	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
1207	            tick = frame.get("tick")
1208	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
1209	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
1210	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
1211	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
1212	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
1213	            if sequence != index + 1:
1214	                raise ValueError(
1215	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
1216	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
1217	                )
1218	            if tick < last_tick:
1219	                raise ValueError(
1220	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
1221	                )
1222	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
1223	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
1224	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
1225	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
1226	            if not added and not removed:
1227	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
1228	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
1229	            if overlap:
1230	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
1231	                raise ValueError(
1232	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
1233	                )
1234	            changes.append(
1235	                {
1236	                    "type": "map_change",
1237	                    "tick": tick,
1238	                    "sequence": sequence,
1239	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1240	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1241	                }
1242	            )
1243	            last_tick = tick
1244	            last_sequence = sequence
1245	        return changes

1247	    @classmethod
1248	    def _validate_map_history(
1249	        cls,
1250	        base_grid: GridMap,
1251	        saved_grid: GridMap,
1252	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
1253	    ) -> None:
1254	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
1255	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height
1256	        for frame in changes:
1257	            for key in ("added", "removed"):
1258	                for cell in frame[key]:
1259	                    x, y = cell
1260	                    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
1261	                        raise ValueError(
1262	                            f"map change {frame['sequence']} cell {list(cell)} lies "
1263	                            "outside the map"
1264	                        )
1265	            added = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"]}
1266	            removed = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"]}
1267	            for cell in added:
1268	                if cell in obstacles:
1269	                    raise ValueError(
1270	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} adds obstacle {list(cell)} "
1271	                        "that is already present according to the history"
1272	                    )
1273	            for cell in removed:
1274	                if cell not in obstacles:
1275	                    raise ValueError(
1276	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} removes obstacle {list(cell)} "
1277	                        "that is absent according to the history"
1278	                    )
1279	            obstacles |= added
1280	            obstacles -= removed
1281	        if obstacles != set(saved_grid.obstacles):
1282	            raise ValueError(
1283	                "the map reproduced from 'map_changes' does not match the saved grid"
1284	            )

1512	    @classmethod
1513	    def _validate_replay_positions(
1514	        cls,
1515	        replay: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
1516	        tick: int,
1517	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
1518	        base_grid: GridMap,
1519	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]] = (),
1520	    ) -> None:
1521	        """Reject history that the simulator could never have produced.
1522	
1523	        Every tick frame is checked against the map in effect *during* that
1524	        tick: positions must be in bounds and traversable, no two robots may
1525	        share a cell, each robot may only wait or step one orthogonal cell
1526	        between consecutive tick frames, two robots may not swap cells within
1527	        one tick, and ``moved`` must list exactly the robots whose positions
1528	        changed.
1529	
1530	        Version 2 map changes take effect after the tick they are stamped on,
1531	        in their recorded order: the frame for tick *t* is judged against the
1532	        base grid plus every change stamped below *t*, then the changes stamped
1533	        *t* are applied and may not add obstacles onto cells frame *t* shows a
1534	        robot on -- even when a later change of the same tick removes the cell
1535	        again. Tick-0 changes precede the first frame. Adjacency is always
1536	        judged between neighboring tick frames; a map change between them never
1537	        moves a robot.
1538	
1539	        Version 1 files pass no changes, so the saved grid governs every frame.
1540	        The first frame has no recorded predecessor: its cells, overlaps and
1541	        ``moved`` ids are still checked, but neither the distance of the first
1542	        moves nor the first ``moved`` list is second-guessed.
1543	        """
1544	        tick_frames = [frame for frame in replay if frame.get("type") == "tick"]
1545	        if len(tick_frames) != tick:
1546	            raise ValueError(
1547	                f"replay has {len(tick_frames)} tick frames but the checkpoint is at tick {tick}"
1548	            )
1549	
1550	        expected_ids = set(robot_by_id)
1551	
1552	        def frame_positions(frame: Mapping[str, object]) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
1553	            raw = frame["robots"]
1554	            assert isinstance(raw, dict)
1555	            if set(raw) != expected_ids:
1556	                raise ValueError(
1557	                    f"replay frame {frame['tick']} robot ids do not match current robots"
1558	                )
1559	            return {robot_id: tuple(position) for robot_id, position in raw.items()}
1560	
1561	        # A non-zero-tick history must end exactly where the saved robots stand
